decisions.statement: A refusal is a 400 with the anthropic error envelope.
A refusal names the error type `invalid_request_error`.
A refusal's message begins `tool_choice forces tool use is not compatible`.
A status other than 400 is no refusal.
A body that will not parse as json is no refusal.
An invalid request with no message is no refusal.
A tool choice of `tool` is rewritten to `auto`.
A tool choice of `any` is rewritten to `auto`.
A tool choice already `auto` is rewritten nowhere.
A body naming no tool choice is rewritten nowhere.
A rewrite has every key the body has beside the tool choice.
A refusal on a body with a forcing tool choice is answered with a retry.
A request that had no body is answered with the response upstream sent.
A 400 that is no refusal is answered with the response upstream sent.
An answer left unchanged has the body text upstream sent.
An answer left unchanged has the status text upstream sent.
An answer left unchanged has the headers upstream sent.
An answer on a trail of one account goes to the seam the caller handed in.
An answer on a longer trail names every account the request reached.
A retry is written about before that retry is answered.
The response body is read to text the once.
Nothing here sends a request.
Nothing here chooses an account.
Nothing here counts the rewrites a request has had.
A rewrite drops the tool a forced choice named.
`tools/lib/model-gateway/forced-tool-choice-rewrite.ts` reads 400 rather than the response's status.
A refusal is read off the message text rather than off a code upstream sends.
The line saying a rewrite happened goes to the console rather than to a seam.

definition: a tool choice upstream refuses to force
